sents.t: The last Monday in May is Memorial Day.
On this day, Americans remember the soldiers who died for their country.
It’s also the unofficial start of summer.
In the morning, Rosa, Lily, and I went to the Memorial Day parade on Main Street.
Old veterans were marching in their uniforms, and the high school band was playing.
People were holding small flags and clapping.
“My father was a soldier,” Rosa told me.
“He served in Vietnam. Every year, I put flowers at the memorial in the park for them.”
At eleven o’clock, everyone stood in silence for one minute.
In the afternoon, the mood changed.
The town pool opened for the summer, and families had picnics in the park.
Danny grilled burgers in Rosa’s backyard, and Carlos and Ana came back from their honeymoon in Mexico with sunburns.
“It’s almost one year since you came to Oakville,” Rosa said.
“What are you going to do this summer?”
“I’m going to start my new job as assistant manager, visit Emma in Chicago, and keep studying English!”
